content.text:
**SAM Template**

Here is a SAM template that you can use to deploy your API:
```yaml
AWSTemplateFormatVersion: '2010-09-09'
Transform: AWS::Serverless-2016-10-31

Resources:
  API:
    Type: AWS::Serverless::Api
    Properties:
      StageName: prod
      Cors:
        AllowHeaders:
          - Content-Type
          - X-Amz-Date
          - Authorization
        AllowMethods:
          - GET
          - POST
          - PUT
          - DELETE
        AllowOrigin: '*'
      DefinitionBody:
        swagger: '2.0'
        info:
          title: My API
          description: My API
          version: 1.0.0
        paths:
          /items:
            get:
              summary: Get items
              description: Get a list of items
              responses:
                200:
                  description: List of items
                  schema:
                    type: array
                    items:
                      $ref: '#/definitions/Item'
            post:
              summary: Create item
              description: Create a new item
              consumes:
                - application/json
              parameters:
                - in: body
                  name: item
                  schema:
                    $ref: '#/definitions/Item'
              responses:
                201:
                  description: Item created
                  schema:
                    $ref: '#/definitions/Item'
          /items/{id}:
            get:
              summary: Get item
              description: Get a specific item
              parameters:
                - in: path
                  name: id
                  required: true
                  type: string
              responses:
                200:
                  description: Item
                  schema:
                    $ref: '#/definitions/Item'
            put:
              summary: Update item
              description: Update a specific item
              parameters:
                - in: path
                  name: id
                  required: true
                  type: string
              consumes:
                - application/json
              parameters:
                - in: body
                  name: item
                  schema:
                    $ref: '#/definitions/Item'
              responses:
                200:
                  description: Item updated
                  schema:
                    $ref: '#/definitions/Item'
            delete:
              summary: Delete item
              description: Delete a specific item
              parameters:
                - in: path
                  name: id
                  required: true
                  type: string
              responses:
                204:
                  description: Item deleted
        definitions:
          Item:
            type: object
            properties:
              id:
                type: string
              name:
                type: string
              description:
                type: string

  ItemsTable:
    Type: AWS::DynamoDB::Table
    Properties:
      TableName: items
      AttributeDefinitions:
        -
          AttributeName: id
          AttributeType: S
        -
          AttributeName: name
          AttributeType: S
        -
          AttributeName: description
          AttributeType: S
      KeySchema:
        -
          AttributeName: id
          KeyType: HASH
        -
          AttributeName: name
          KeyType: RANGE
      ProvisionedThroughput:
        ReadCapacityUnits: 1
        WriteCapacityUnits: 1

Outputs:
  API:
    Value: !Sub "https://${AWS::Region}.execute-api.${AWS::Region}.amazonaws.com/prod/items"
    Description: API endpoint
```
This template defines a Serverless API with a single resource, `API`, which is a RESTful API that exposes a single endpoint, `GET /items`. The API uses a DynamoDB table, `ItemsTable`, to store items.

Note that this is just a basic template, and you may need to modify it to fit your specific use case.

**SAM Init**

To initialize a new SAM project, you can run the following command:
```bash
sam init
```
This will create a new directory with the basic structure for a SAM project. You can then modify the template to fit your specific needs.
